headline: Per reporting from @KyivIndependent, Ukraine has effectively exhausted its supply of Patriot PAC-3 interceptors, leaving Kyiv with little ability to defend against Russia's ballistic missile attacks. During Russia's latest large-scale strike, Ukrainian officials say 23 ballistic missiles and six 3M22 Zircon hypersonic missiles reached their targets, while air defenses were still able to intercept 37 cruise missiles and 326 drones. Ukrainian officials attribute the disparity to a shortage of PAC-3 interceptors, which remain one of the few systems capable of defeating ballistic missiles. The shortage comes as global demand for Patriot interceptors has surged, with U.S. inventories strained by commitments in the Middle East and elsewhere. As a result, Russia appears to be placing increasing emphasis on ballistic missile strikes against Ukrainian cities and critical infrastructure.

headline: According to the Associated Press, two Tennessee National Guard soldiers assigned to the Trump administration's Memphis Safe Task Force fatally shot an armed man during a foot pursuit early Sunday morning. Authorities say the soldiers, who were assisting Memphis Police in responding to reports of gunfire, opened fire after the suspect allegedly turned toward them with a firearm. The suspect was pronounced dead at the scene despite life-saving efforts by two National Guard medical specialists. No law enforcement personnel were injured. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation is leading the investigation. The incident marks the first fatal shooting involving National Guard personnel deployed under the administration's crime-reduction mission in Memphis, where the federal deployment has faced legal and political opposition since it began last year.
